text: You buy airtime. Your account is debited. The airtime never lands. Then you spend two weeks chasing a refund.
Every day, millions of us top up phones and prepaid meters. When the money moves first and the product comes later, all the risk is on us.
This is Con-fam. E no land? You no pay. You pay for airtime, data and electricity with Bitcoin, and your payment only completes after the provider confirms delivery.
Connect a wallet. For this demo, a free test wallet with twenty five thousand test sats.
Pick airtime. Enter the number, the network and the amount. Con-fam shows the exact price in sats.
Now watch. My sats are locked, not sent. A hold invoice keeps them in the Lightning network, and Con-fam cannot take them yet.
Con-fam buys the airtime. Only when the provider confirms delivery does the payment complete.
And I get a receipt signed with Nostr, checked right here in my browser.
Now the bad day. This purchase fails. The lock opens by itself. Not charged. My sats never left my wallet. No refund to chase, no support ticket.
And in Dakar, the same guarantee for Woyofal electricity, in French, in C F A, with the token on screen.
Airtime in nineteen African countries, data in thirteen, and electricity in Nigeria and Senegal.
We measure it in public. Delivery rate. Time to delivery. And the number that matters most, charged without delivery. Zero.
Next, real money on our own Lightning node, TV and water bills, automatic meter top ups, and agents who accept sats on the street.
Con-fam. E no land? You no pay.
